title: Daily Devotional #63
paragraphs: As I reflect on Luke 19, I am struck by the story of Zacchaeus, the chief tax collector, who climbed a sycamore tree to see Jesus. Despite his wealth and power, Zacchaeus recognized that he needed something more in his life. He was willing to take a risk and do something unconventional to encounter you.

Lord, I pray that I can have the same boldness and courage to seek you out, even when it means stepping out of my comfort zone. Help me to recognize the things in my life that are hindering my relationship with you and give me the strength to let them go.

In this chapter, Jesus also tells the parable of the ten minas, where a nobleman goes on a journey and entrusts his servants with his wealth. The servants who invested wisely were rewarded, but the one who did not invest was punished.
Lord, I am reminded that you have given me gifts and talents to use for your glory. Help me to be a good steward of what you have entrusted to me and to use it to further your kingdom.
Finally, in this chapter, Jesus enters Jerusalem triumphantly, fulfilling the prophecy of Zechariah. The people were filled with joy and praised God, but Jesus wept because he knew what was to come.

Lord, help me to remember that even in the midst of our earthly triumphs, there is still pain and suffering in this world. Remind me to have compassion for those who are hurting and to be a light in the darkness.
Thank you, Lord, for the lessons in Luke 19. May they continue to guide me in my faith journey.
